title: Release audit: The session keeps unredacted engine text in memory. `show_state` assigns the raw
summary: Store the redacted form, or a hash, for comparison and deduplication, and never assign raw engine text to long-lived session attributes.
requirements: Any text produced by the engine that the client keeps in memory for the session is masked before it is kept, so the in-memory copy never contains a value the client would mask on screen.
The retained state text shown by the state display is the masked text; repeating the display later does not reveal the secret.
The retained idle-refresh failure text is masked before retention, and any later display of that failure shows only the mask.
Masking applies equally to engine answers and engine error messages.
Text that carries no key material is retained and shown unchanged, apart from the masking applied today.
Masking an already-masked retained text leaves it unchanged: no second marker appears and no content is lost.
What the user sees on a later repeat of retained text equals what the client retained; there is no path where the retained copy is more revealing than the display.
No other client behavior changes, and the existing test suite passes.
acceptance: When the engine returns an answer whose text contains key material, nothing the client retains for the session contains that value in readable form; the user sees only the mask.
When the engine fails with an error message containing key material, the failure text the client retains and any later display of it contain only the mask.
An answer or error without key material is retained and shown exactly as before.
Masking retained text a second time yields the same text, with one marker per masked value.
Repeating a retained state or failure display later shows the same masked text that was retained.

external_dependencies.name: Forgel engine commands
external_dependencies.interface: Invoke the Forgel engine command interface exposed by the project’s `main` application repository: pass a command name and parameters, receive the returned text answer, and on failure catch the engine error and read `message`. Both the text and the error message must be masked before retention.
external_dependencies.docs: Project repository list; FORGEL.md — Runtime Process Model and D-108.
external_dependencies.evidence: The project repository contract lists the Forgel application repositories (`main: application`, `code: application`). FORGEL.md states the runtime is code-owned in `src/forgel/runtime_model.py` and that runtime operations are directly available (D-108: `drive`, `task ...`, `release ...`). The task dependency contract defines the engine invocation result as a text answer or an error `message`.

result.summary: The interactive session now masks engine-derived text before it is retained in memory. `show_state` builds the state text with `redact(...)` before comparing it to and storing it in `last_state`, and the forced refresh path in `refresh` stores `redact(...)` as well, so the retained state equals what the screen showed and a later repeat only shows the mask. `idle_refresh` masks the engine error message (`redact(exc.message)`) before keeping it in `idle_failure`; the once-per-message comparison uses the masked text, so an already-masked retained failure stays unchanged and the displayed text is the retained text. Secret-free text is unaffected because `redact` is idempotent and returns it unchanged. Added `tests/test_retained_text.py`, which drives real stub engine processes and asserts that retained state and retained idle failure contain no readable secret, that a repeat of the retained text shows the same masked text, that re-masking leaves it unchanged, and that secret-free state is retained and shown exactly as before. Full suite: `python -m pytest -q` -> 314 passed, 293 subtests passed.
assumptions: The two engine-derived texts the client keeps for the session are the last state text and the last idle-refresh failure text, as named in the audit finding; no other engine text is retained, so only these two sites needed masking.
The existing `redact` routine is reused unchanged; masking rules, the mask marker and the secret label set stay as they are.

An answer or error without key material is retained and shown exactly as before.

review.summary: The attributed change does exactly what the release-audit finding requires: `show_state`, the forced branch of `refresh`, and `idle_refresh` now mask engine-produced text with the existing `redact` routine before it is stored in `last_state` / `idle_failure`, so the in-memory copy equals what the screen showed and a later repeat cannot reveal a secret. Display paths are unchanged and are shown by the new tests to already mask, so displayed and retained text coincide. Secret-free text keeps its previous form because `redact` leaves it untouched, and the new tests explicitly assert idempotence of `redact` on the retained copy (AC-4). The change is scoped to the two reported retention points named in the specification's assumptions, does not touch masking rules, the marker, the parsed answer, or persist anything, and adds regression coverage for both engine answers and engine errors (FR-4). The added test file is real product regression coverage, not a documentation guard, and no pre-existing test was removed or weakened. The environment gate and the listed acceptance checks pass.

requirements.requirement: FR-1: Any text produced by the engine that the client keeps in memory for the session is masked before it is kept (state text and idle-refresh failure text).
requirements.note: `show_state` stores `redact("\n".join(lines))`, `refresh(force=True)` stores `redact(...)`, and `idle_refresh` stores `redact(exc.message)`; the specification's assumption names these two as the only engine-derived retained texts.

requirements.requirement: FR-2: The retained state text shown by the state display is the masked text; repeating the display later does not reveal the secret.
requirements.note: The same masked string is both stored in `last_state` and written, so a later repeat of the retained text stays masked; covered by `test_repeating_a_retained_state_display_shows_the_mask`.

requirements.requirement: FR-3: The retained idle-refresh failure text is masked before retention and any later display shows only the mask.
requirements.note: `failure = redact(exc.message)` is compared and stored, and `show_failure` is exercised by a test that asserts no readable secret reaches the output.

requirements.requirement: FR-4: Masking applies equally to engine answers and engine error messages.
requirements.note: State text (answer-derived) and `EngineError` messages are both redacted; regression tests cover both a secret-bearing state and a secret-bearing error.

requirements.requirement: FR-5: Text that carries no key material is retained and shown unchanged, apart from the masking applied today.
requirements.note: `redact` is applied to the same text as before and is the pre-existing routine; `test_secret_free_state_is_retained_unchanged` asserts byte-identical retention and display for a clean state.

requirements.requirement: FR-6: Masking an already-masked retained text leaves it unchanged, with one marker per masked value.
requirements.note: Retained copies are asserted equal to their own re-redaction in both the state and failure tests, confirming no stacked marker and no content loss.

requirements.requirement: FR-7: What the user sees on a later repeat equals what the client retained; no path where the retained copy is more revealing than the display.
requirements.note: Retention now uses exactly the displayed (masked) string in every touched path; the tests assert absence of the raw value in both the retained attribute and the output.

requirements.requirement: FR-8: No other client behavior changes and the existing test suite passes.
requirements.note: Only the three retention points changed; deduplication now compares masked messages, which for secret-free text is identical to before. Environment gate and listed acceptance checks report pass, and no test was removed.

requirements.requirement: AC-1/AC-2/AC-3/AC-4/AC-5: Acceptance criteria for secret-bearing answers, secret-bearing errors, secret-free text, idempotent re-masking and repeated displays.
requirements.note: Each criterion has a matching assertion in tests/test_retained_text.py, and the acceptance checks for the masked-answer and secret-free cases are recorded as passing.
QA verdict is pass; no test removals were detected in the attributed commit.

requirements.requirement: Non-goals/constraints: no change to masking rules, marker or secret labels, no change to engine requests or parsing, no persistence, no new stored artifact, no unrelated refactor or new interface.
requirements.note: The diff only wraps existing masked text at retention points and adds one focused test module; nothing else in the client is touched.

requirements.requirement: No unrelated, temporary, debug or generated files in the change, and every needed file present.
requirements.note: The commit contains only forgel_code/interactive.py and the new tests/test_retained_text.py; the worktree is clean and no escalated changes exist.
